overview: Czechia, also called the Czech Republic, is a landlocked country in Central Europe. Its capital, Prague, is known for its medieval old town and its castle. Czechoslovakia split peacefully into Czechia and Slovakia on 1 January 1993. Czechia joined NATO in 1999 and the European Union in 2004.

geography.text: Czechia is made up of two main historic lands: Bohemia in the west, a basin ringed by low mountains, and Moravia in the east. The Vltava flows through Prague and joins the Elbe, which carries water north through Germany to the North Sea. The highest mountains are along the borders, including the Krkonoše range on the border with Poland.

history.text: Bohemia was a powerful kingdom in the Middle Ages, and under Charles IV Prague was the capital of the Holy Roman Empire. From 1526 the Czech lands were ruled by the Habsburgs. Czechoslovakia was created in 1918, occupied by Nazi Germany and then ruled by communists, until the peaceful Velvet Revolution of 1989. In 1993 it split peacefully into two countries.

events.title: Charles University
events.text: The first university in central Europe is founded in Prague.

events.title: Defenestration of Prague
events.text: Officials are thrown from a castle window, sparking the Thirty Years' War.

events.title: Czechoslovakia founded
events.text: Czechs and Slovaks form a new country after the First World War.

events.title: Prague Spring
events.text: Reforms are crushed by a Soviet-led invasion.

events.title: Velvet Divorce
events.text: Czechoslovakia splits peacefully into Czechia and Slovakia.
